chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal said:

Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding Ibn Asbat, saying to him: 'What do you think regarding him?' Ibn Asbat was present, and we were all traveling by sea or by land to Egypt. He informed him about the news of the land route. He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go to the mosque at a time other than that of a compulsory prayer, pray two rak'ahs, and seek guidance from Allah a hundred times. Then see what comes to your heart and act upon it.' Al-Hasan said to him, 'The land route is more preferable to me.' He said, 'And to me as well.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform the prayer of guidance (Salat al-Istikhara) according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (or Imam al-Hadi, depending on the specific chain interpretation of al-Jahm) highlights the spiritual discipline of Istikhara during travel, emphasizing the purification of intention through repeated supplication. The Imam’s affirmation that the land route was preferable to him personally adds a layer of scholarly nuance, suggesting that while the heart's inclination is key, it is often aligned with the Imam’s own spiritual insight or the objective best interest (maslaha) of the traveler.
